claims.text: The starting eutectic high-entropy alloy has a hierarchical dual-phase lamellar microstructure containing a ductile fcc phase and a hard B2 phase.
Dislocation pile-ups at fcc/B2 interfaces generate high local stress concentrations, microcracking, and premature failure.
Moderate-temperature annealing can selectively recrystallize the ductile fcc phase.
The selective annealing treatment can preserve the integrity of the hard B2 phase.
The treatment will produce a fully or partially recrystallized soft fcc phase embedded in a stable hard B2 phase.
The treated microstructure will exhibit more uniform lamellar deformation and stabilized internal boundaries.
Selective recrystallization introduces new, finer fcc grains that reduce the density of pre-existing dislocation pile-ups at fcc/B2 interfaces.
The recrystallized fcc phase accommodates plastic deformation more uniformly.
Reducing interfacial dislocation pile-ups relieves local stress concentrations.
The combined reduction in stress concentration and enhancement of back-stress hardening will increase tensile ductility while retaining or increasing yield and ultimate tensile strength.
The treated alloy may achieve approximately 35% or greater uniform elongation.
The treated alloy may reach a true tensile stress of approximately 2 GPa.
The untreated eutectic alloy has limited room-temperature ductility because of dislocation accumulation at dual-phase interfaces and associated microcracking.
The proposed comparison applies to quasi-static room-temperature tensile loading at a conventional strain rate around 10^-3 s^-1.
Avoiding coarsening of the hard B2 phase is critical to preserving the proposed strength-ductility balance.
The strength-ductility balance may vary with annealing temperature and time.
The hypothesis can be tested by comparing annealed and untreated samples from the same alloy using microscopy, dislocation characterization, and room-temperature tensile tests.
Failure to improve ductility to the stated criterion, or any reduction of yield or ultimate tensile strength below the untreated baseline, is designated as a falsifying outcome.
